formation.title: The Birth of Russia
formation.text:
The scattered principalities of the Rus have been gathered under one sovereign. Moscow, Novgorod, Tver and Vladimir obey one throne, and its holder is styled Sovereign of All Rus. It is a kingdom among kingdoms and not yet an empire: a tsar's crown is still to be claimed, and what kind of realm will claim it is disputed.

The Orthodox clergy speak of Moscow as the Third Rome, the last bastion of true Christianity, destined to lead the faithful until the end of days. The sovereign's authority, they argue, derives from God alone, and the realm's purpose is to be the guardian of Orthodoxy.

Others look east, beyond the Stone, as the Urals are called, to the forests of Siberia, where fortunes are measured in furs and the land has no end. The Cossacks and frontiersmen who push the border further need not priests but powder and provisions. They see a realm that grows by conquest and trade until it reaches the ocean.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Moscow is the Third Rome. There shall be no fourth.

modifiers.name: Third Rome Ascendant
modifiers.text: Moscow stands as the successor to Rome and Constantinople, the last guardian of true Orthodox Christianity. Its sovereign rules as God's chosen vessel on earth, and from this sacred authority flows the power to hold all the Russian lands under a single crown.

options.text: Our road lies east, beyond the Stone and on to the ocean.

modifiers.name: Beyond the Stone
modifiers.text: Russia's future lies not in the cramped courts of Europe but beyond the Stone, as the Urals are called, in the forests and rivers that run east to the ocean. The Cossack and the fur trapper carry Moscow's banner into the wilderness, and every river crossed and every stockade raised extends the realm.

advances.name: Druzhina Tradition
advances.text: The druzhina (the personal retinue of mounted warriors serving the prince) forms the core of early Russian military power: sworn household men who ride to war beside their lord and sit in his council in peace.

advances.name: Charters of Governance
advances.text: When a land comes under Moscow, the grand prince gives it a charter: what the governor may take for his keep, what each fine is, and how a thief or a murderer is tried. The Dvina land received such a charter in 1397. A land that knows what it owes is slower to rise.

advances.name: Northern Thebaid
advances.text: In 1337 Sergius of Radonezh raises a wooden church to the Trinity in the forest north of Moscow. His disciples carry the rule further into the wilderness, founding hermitage after hermitage from Beloozero to the White Sea, and peasants follow the monks into land no prince had ever taxed.

advances.name: Fur Trade Foundations
advances.text: Russia's northern forests yield an abundance of sable, fox, and ermine, forming the backbone of early Russian commerce and drawing merchants from as far as Constantinople and the Islamic world.

advances.name: Gathering of the Russian Lands
advances.text: Under Ivan III, Moscow systematically absorbs the independent Russian principalities (Novgorod, Tver, Yaroslavl, Rostov), forging a unified state from the patchwork of medieval appanages.

advances.name: Third Rome
advances.text: After the fall of Constantinople in 1453, Moscow claims the mantle of the Third Rome: the last guardian of Orthodox Christianity, with its sovereign as God's representative on earth.

advances.name: Scribe Books
advances.text: The grand prince's scribes ride through each newly gathered land and write down every village, every plough and every due, as they did in the lands of Novgorod in the 1490s. The scribe books tell Moscow what a district owes and who holds it, and no local custom can be pleaded against them.

advances.name: Gostiny Dvor Tradition
advances.text: The gostiny dvor (merchant courts where traders from across Russia and foreign lands gather to conduct business) becomes a cornerstone of Russian commercial life, regulated by the state for order and revenue.

advances.name: Town Stewards
advances.text: In each fortified town a steward is chosen from the service gentry of the district to see to its walls, its store of powder and shot, and the dues that pay for them. When raiders come, the countryside shelters in the yards kept within the walls.

advances.name: Pomestye Service Estates
advances.text: The pomestye system grants conditional land estates to military servitors in exchange for mounted service, creating a new class of service nobles bound to the sovereign's army.

advances.name: Boyar Duma
advances.text: The Boyar Duma, an advisory council of the highest-ranking nobles and clergy, deliberates on matters of state, war, and law at the sovereign's pleasure.

advances.name: Streltsy Corps
advances.text: Ivan IV establishes the Streltsy, Russia's first permanent standing infantry armed with firearms. Salaried and uniformed, they represent a decisive step toward a professional army.

event.title: The Streltsy Corps
event.text:
A new kind of soldier marches through the streets of Moscow. Armed with matchlock muskets and heavy bardiches, the Streltsy are Russia's first permanent standing infantry, salaried, uniformed, and drilled in the use of firearms. Unlike the feudal cavalry of the boyars, these men owe their loyalty directly to the Tsar. Initially numbering some three thousand, the corps has grown to garrison every major city, their distinctive colored coats becoming a symbol of centralized military power.

The question now is how to employ them. As a disciplined field force, trained in European-style volley fire and capable of standing against any army on the continent? Or as garrison troops, manning the walls of Russian cities and frontier fortresses, providing the backbone of the realm's defensive network?

options.text: Train them as a professional field army.

modifiers.name: Streltsy Field Discipline
modifiers.text: The Streltsy corps is trained as a professional field army, drilled in volley fire and disciplined maneuver.

options.text: Station them as the realm's garrison backbone.

modifiers.name: Streltsy Garrison Network
modifiers.text: The Streltsy garrisons provide a permanent defensive backbone across the realm's cities and fortresses.

advances.name: The Chosen Thousand
advances.text: In 1550 Ivan IV orders a thousand of his best servitors settled on estates within reach of Moscow, to be at hand for any errand of the crown. They owe their land to the tsar alone. From picked men of this kind he later draws the black-clad horsemen of his own household.

event.title: The Chosen Thousand
event.text:
A thousand picked servitors have been settled on estates within reach of Moscow. They hold their land of the tsar alone and stand ready for any errand of the crown: an embassy, a command, an inquiry into a governor's accounts.

The great houses watch them with unease. Men who owe everything to one master can be turned against anyone. Some at court urge that they be made the tsar's own household, set apart from the boyar council and answering to no court but his. Others hold that they should serve within the old order, in the offices and regiments where the realm is short of able men.

options.text: They are the tsar's men alone. Let them watch the great houses.

modifiers.name: The Tsar's Own Household
modifiers.text: The chosen servitors answer to the tsar alone. The great houses are watched, and no boyar or province is beyond their reach.

options.text: Let them serve in the offices and the regiments, under the old order.

modifiers.name: Servitors Within the Old Order
modifiers.text: The chosen servitors are spread through the offices and commands of the realm. Able men serve beside the boyars, and the council governs without fear.

advances.name: Siberian Conquest
advances.text: The conquest of the Khanate of Sibir opens the way to the vast wilderness beyond the Urals, where Cossack explorers and fur traders push the frontier ever eastward toward the Pacific. They coast the Arctic shore and work the great rivers in the koch, the round-hulled boat of the Pomors that the ice lifts instead of crushing.

advances.name: Orthodox Cultural Renaissance
advances.text: Russian icon painting, church architecture, and liturgical music reach new heights of artistic achievement, creating a distinctive Orthodox cultural tradition that rivals the art of Byzantium itself.

advances.name: Smuta Resilience
advances.text: The Time of Troubles tests Russia to its breaking point (famine, invasion, civil war, and pretenders to the throne), but the nation endures, emerging with a deepened sense of national identity and resilience.

advances.name: Grain Spirits Industry
advances.text: Russian distillers perfect the production of grain-based spirits, creating a domestic industry that generates significant revenue for the state treasury through monopoly sales.

advances.name: Cossack Hosts
advances.text: The semi-autonomous Cossack communities of the Don, Zaporozhian Sich, and Yaik are formalized as military hosts, giving the Tsar superb light cavalry in exchange for land and self-governance.

advances.name: Zemsky Sobor
advances.text: The Assembly of the Land. The tsar calls the boyars, the clergy, the service gentry and the townsmen together to hear what the realm will bear. In 1613 the assembly chooses Michael Romanov as tsar, and through his reign it sits year after year and votes the taxes for his wars.

advances.name: Patriarchate of Moscow
advances.text: The establishment of the Patriarchate of Moscow in 1589 elevates the Russian Church to full independence, confirming Moscow's spiritual authority over all Orthodox believers.

advances.name: New Formation Regiments
advances.text: European-trained officers drill Russian soldiers in Western military methods, creating 'new formation' regiments of infantry, dragoons, and reiters that supplement the traditional Streltsy and feudal cavalry.

advances.name: Ural Ironworks
advances.text: The Ural Mountains yield vast deposits of iron ore, and the establishment of state-sponsored foundries transforms Russia into one of Europe's largest producers of iron and cannon.

advances.name: White Settlements Abolished
advances.text: After the Moscow rising of 1648 the tax free suburbs that boyars and monasteries keep beside the towns are taken from them. Their craftsmen and traders are entered among the tsar's own townsmen and pay with them. The towns are quiet, and their dues go to the crown.

advances.name: Don Cossack Host
advances.text: The Don Cossacks are formally recognized as a military estate of the realm, providing elite light cavalry for the Tsar's campaigns in exchange for autonomy on their ancestral lands along the Don River.

advances.name: Petrine Naval Reforms
advances.text: Peter the Great, having labored as an apprentice shipwright in Dutch and English dockyards, returns to build Russia a navy from nothing: establishing naval academies, dockyards, and the new capital of St. Petersburg as a window to the sea.

advances.name: Baltic Fleet
advances.text: The creation of the Baltic Fleet transforms Russia from a landlocked power into a naval force capable of contesting the Baltic Sea, challenging Swedish dominance and securing Russia's access to European trade.

advances.name: Heraldmaster's Office
advances.text: The Heraldmaster's office, set under the Senate in 1722 with Stepan Kolychev at its head, keeps the roll of every man in the sovereign's service, sees that no noble evades it, and enters among the nobility the commoners whose rank has earned it.

event.title: The Heraldmaster's Office
event.text:
A Heraldmaster has been set under the Senate with a single task: to know every man who owes service. His clerks draw up the rolls of the nobility, find out who is hiding on his estates, and enter among the nobles the commoners whose rank has earned it. Coats of arms are drawn for families that never had one.

The old boyar families are outraged to see the sons of clerks inscribed beside them. But the state needs able officers and administrators, and now it knows where to find them: a new service nobility whose loyalty is to the state and not to clan or tradition.

options.text: Merit shall be the measure of a man.

advances.name: Guberniya System
advances.text: The realm is reorganized into guberniyas (provinces governed by appointed governors answerable directly to the central government), replacing the old patchwork of local administration.

advances.name: Military Colonization
advances.text: Soldier-settlers are established in frontier regions, combining military duty with agricultural cultivation to provide both defense and sustenance for the expanding realm.

advances.name: Suvorov's Military School
advances.text: Alexander Suvorov's doctrines of speed, aggression, and bayonet assault produce a generation of elite grenadiers who fight with unmatched ferocity and tactical initiative.

event.title: The Science of Victory
event.text:
General Alexander Suvorov has transformed Russian military doctrine with his treatise 'The Science of Victory.' His principles are brutally simple: train relentlessly, move fast, strike with the bayonet. 'The bullet is a fool, the bayonet a fine fellow,' he teaches his grenadiers. His campaigns have proven the doctrine sound: undefeated in over sixty battles, Suvorov's soldiers march faster, hit harder, and fight with a fury that confounds their enemies.

His methods emphasize speed over caution, attack over defense, and the initiative of individual soldiers over rigid formation drill. Russian grenadiers trained in his school are among the finest infantry in Europe.

advances.name: Great Power Diplomacy
advances.text: Russia's emergence as a European great power demands a sophisticated diplomatic corps, and Russia now maintains ambassadors at every major court, wielding influence from Paris to Constantinople.

advances.name: Russian Enlightenment
advances.text: Catherine the Great corresponds with Voltaire and Diderot, establishes the Free Economic Society, and founds schools across the country. Russian letters, science, and philosophy flourish as never before.

advances.name: Industrial Dawn
advances.text:
The first stirrings of industrialization reach Russia as mechanized production begins in textiles and metalworking, and state-sponsored factories multiply across the Urals and around Moscow. The arms works at Izhevsk and Zlatoust turn Ural steel into muskets and blades for the army.

Available in: Ural Ironworks

destiny.name: Sovereign of All Rus
destiny.text: Russia has been forged from the scattered principalities of the Rus. Now its sovereign must show that the new state has the stability and authority to endure. Only a realm at peace with itself can pursue the ambitions that lie ahead, a tsar's crown among them.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: Sovereign of All Rus
event.text:
The Russian state has achieved a measure of stability that few thought possible in these turbulent lands. The boyars have been brought to heel, the Church blesses the sovereign's authority, and the common people look to Moscow as the center of their world. This stability is not an end but a beginning: the foundation on which an empire may yet be proclaimed.

The question now is what Russia shall become.

destiny.name: Return of the Mother Cities
destiny.text: Reclaim Kyiv, the baptismal cradle of the Rus, and Vilnius, capital of the Grand Duchy that challenged Moscow's claim to Orthodox supremacy. Both must be won in the west by force of arms.

conditions.text: Chose the Third Rome Ascendant destiny
Own Kyiv, or a subject owns it
Own Vilnius, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Return of the Mother Cities
event.text:
Kyiv, where Grand Prince Vladimir received baptism and brought Christianity to the Rus, has been restored to the Russian realm. Vilnius, capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania (Russia's oldest rival for dominion over the Orthodox east), has fallen to Moscow's armies. These are not mere conquests but the assertion of a civilizational claim.

Pilgrims flock to the Monastery of the Caves in Kyiv, and the churches ring with celebration. Russia's claim as the guardian of Orthodoxy is strengthened immeasurably by the return of these cities to her sphere.

destiny.name: The Baltic Window
destiny.text: Seize the great Baltic ports of Riga and Tallinn to break through to European maritime trade; the window opens no earlier than the Age of Reformation. Amass the treasury required to sustain a westward-facing realm.

conditions.text: Own Riga, or a subject owns it
Own Tallinn, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000
Reformation or later

event.title: The Baltic Breakthrough
event.text:
The great ports of Riga and Tallinn are now Russian. For the first time, Russia has direct access to European maritime trade routes, and Russian merchants can deal with Hamburg, Amsterdam, and London without intermediaries. The Baltic is no longer a Swedish or Hanseatic lake.

This breakthrough poses a fundamental question for the country. Should Russia embrace the ways of Europe (its courts, its fashions, its diplomatic culture) and take its place as a European great power? Or should the Third Rome stand apart, a fortress of Orthodox faith and Russian tradition, drawing strength from its distinctiveness rather than conformity?

options.text: Open the doors to European civilization.

modifiers.name: European Window
modifiers.text: Russia opens its doors to European culture, commerce, and ideas, embracing the wider world beyond the Orthodox sphere.

options.text: We are the fortress of the true faith.

modifiers.name: Orthodox Bastion
modifiers.text: The Third Rome stands apart from the Latin and Protestant West, drawing strength from the purity of its Orthodox faith and the unity of its people.

destiny.name: The Third Rome Ascends
destiny.text: Take Constantinople itself and restore the Hagia Sophia to Orthodox worship. Only a powerful and renowned realm can claim the mantle of Rome.

conditions.text: Own Constantinople, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 75
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Third Rome Ascends
event.text:
The unthinkable has been achieved. The double-headed eagle flies above the walls of Constantinople, and the great dome of the Hagia Sophia once again resounds with Orthodox liturgy. The prophecy of the monk Filofey is fulfilled: Moscow, the Third Rome, has reclaimed the Second.

The ruler of Russia now stands as the supreme leader of the Orthodox world, protector of millions of believers from the Balkans to the Caucasus. But how shall this universal authority be exercised? Through the spiritual prestige of the Ecumenical Throne, absorbing the Orthodox peoples into a commonwealth of faith? Or through the iron authority of a new Caesar, whose military might enforces the peace?

options.text: We shall unite the faithful under one throne.

modifiers.name: Ecumenical Throne
modifiers.text: The ruler of Russia sits upon the Ecumenical Throne, spiritual father of all Orthodox Christians, wielding the soft power of faith to bind nations in a commonwealth of believers.

options.text: Let the world tremble before the new Caesar.

modifiers.name: The New Caesar
modifiers.text: A new Roman Emperor has risen in the East, and the world trembles before the military might of the Third Rome restored.

destiny.name: The Eastern Road
destiny.text: Conquer Kazan, which blocks the route east, and seize Tobolsk, gateway to Siberia. Hold both, and the road into Siberia lies open.

conditions.text: Chose the Beyond the Stone destiny
Own Kazan, or a subject owns it
Own Tobolsk, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Eastern Road Opens
event.text:
Russian forces have crossed the Ural Mountains and seized Tobolsk, capital of the Siberian Khanate. The Khanate of Kazan, which long blocked the eastern road, has been subdued. The way into the boundless Siberian wilderness lies open.

Cossack scouts report rivers teeming with fish, forests dark with sable, and vast grasslands stretching to horizons beyond counting. An entire continent awaits not merely Moscow's flag but Russian settlers, institutions, and commerce.

destiny.name: Siberian Wealth
destiny.text: Let Tobolsk, the stockade above the Irtysh, grow into the capital town of Siberia. Build a fur trade that feeds the markets of Moscow and the world. Let the monks go into the taiga and found three forest hermitages, so that the church reaches the frontier.

conditions.text: At least 3 of our locations have a Forest Hermitage
We own Tobolsk and it has grown into a town or a city
A market the country is in

children.text: Fur is produced in the market
Fur is traded in the market

event.title: The Wealth of Siberia
event.text:
Russia's vast eastern territories have begun to yield their riches in earnest. Fur caravans stretch from the taiga to Moscow, the bells of forest hermitages ring beyond the Urals, Tobolsk has grown into a town, and Russian settlements dot the river systems from the Urals to the Yenisey. Siberia is no longer merely conquered: it is becoming productive.

The question now is how to extract and organize this wealth. The yasak system of fur tribute, imposed on native peoples in exchange for nominal protection, funnels enormous wealth to the treasury but at the cost of local stability. Alternatively, encouraging mass Russian settlement would permanently integrate Siberia but require a different investment in roads, farms, and administration.

options.text: Impose the yasak. Siberia shall pay its tribute.

modifiers.name: Yasak Tribute System
modifiers.text: The yasak system extracts fur tribute from Siberian peoples, funneling vast wealth to Moscow at the cost of local relations with the conquered.

options.text: Send settlers. Siberia shall become Russia.

modifiers.name: Settler Colonization
modifiers.text: Russian settlers pour eastward in great waves, establishing permanent villages and farms that bind Siberia irrevocably to the motherland.

destiny.name: Continental Colossus
destiny.text: Carry the Russian state to the far side of Siberia. Irkutsk, on the road to Lake Baikal, must grow from a stockade into a town. Ironworks must rise in three Russian towns to cast the iron of a continent, the treasury must overflow, and the world must recognize Russian greatness.

conditions.text: At least 3 of our locations have Ural Ironworks
We own Irkutsk and it has grown into a town or a city
Gold at least 3000
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Continental Colossus
event.text:
Russia has achieved what no empire in history has matched: a continental domain stretching across eleven time zones, developed and administered, its institutions reaching from the Baltic to the Pacific watershed. Ural iron arms its regiments and roofs its cities, and the treasury reflects the wealth of a hundred peoples and a thousand rivers.

This colossus faces a fundamental choice in how to wield its continental mass. As a land power without equal, Russia can dominate the Eurasian heartland through sheer territorial depth and military doctrine. Or Russia can look beyond the continent, building a Pacific fleet to project power across the ocean and engage with the maritime civilizations of East Asia.

options.text: We are the lords of the continent.

modifiers.name: Heartland Power
modifiers.text: Russia commands the Eurasian heartland, its armies sustained by continental depth and strategic doctrine that renders naval power irrelevant.

options.text: Build a Pacific fleet. The ocean is next.

modifiers.name: Pacific Horizon
modifiers.text: Russia builds a Pacific fleet and looks beyond the continent, engaging with the maritime civilizations of East Asia while neglecting some domestic construction.

units.name: Druzhina
units.text: The prince's own retinue: mailed horsemen sworn to him in person, who carry the bow of the steppe beside the lance and the sword.

units.name: Pomestnoe Voysko
units.text: The landed army of Muscovy. Every service estate sends its riders in quilted coats with bow, quiver and sabre. No host in the east musters more horsemen, and none is quicker to ride home at harvest.

units.name: Streltsy
units.text: Moscow's standing musket infantry, uniformed and salaried, armed with matchlock firearms and heavy bardiches. The backbone of Russian military power in the age of gunpowder.

units.name: Cossack Light Cavalry
units.text: Steppe horsemen from the frontier communities, expert riders and raiders who serve as the Tsar's eyes and ears across the vast southern borderlands. They ride round an enemy and do not stand in front of one.

units.name: Oprichnik Cavalry
units.text: The Tsar's personal enforcers, black-clad horsemen who carry a dog's head and broom at their saddle, symbols of their mission to sniff out and sweep away treason.

units.name: Don Cossack
units.text: Elite horsemen of the Don Cossack Host, veteran cavalrymen who combine steppe riding traditions with disciplined military service to the crown.

units.name: Suvorov Grenadier
units.text: Elite infantry trained in Suvorov's doctrine of speed and bayonet assault. 'The bullet is a fool, the bayonet a fine fellow.' These men embody that creed.

units.name: Baltic Frigate
units.text: A fast warship of the Russian Baltic Fleet, built in the new dockyards of St. Petersburg to contest Swedish dominance of the northern seas.

units.name: Soldaty of the New Order
units.text: Foot regiments drilled in pike and shot by hired Scottish, Dutch and German colonels. They hold a line as no gentry levy can, for as long as the conscripts in the ranks stay with the colours.

units.name: Koch
units.text: The ice boat of the Pomors: a round hull with a second skin of larch at the waterline, one mast and one square sail. A dozen men sail it and it carries forty more. Slow and almost unarmed, it goes where no other ship can follow.

buildings.name: Gostiny Dvor
buildings.text: A merchant court where traders from across Russia and foreign lands gather to sell their wares under state regulation, fostering orderly commerce and tax collection.

buildings.name: Siege Yard
buildings.text: A yard kept inside the walls of a fortified town by the landholders of its district, with a caretaker in peace and room for their households, grain and arms in war. The town steward sees that the walls, the guns and the yards are ready.

buildings.name: Ural Ironworks
buildings.text: A state-sponsored iron foundry in the Ural Mountains, smelting the region's vast ore deposits into iron and steel for the state's arsenals.

buildings.name: Naval Academy
buildings.text: A school of navigation and shipbuilding established in the Petrine tradition, training officers and craftsmen to build and sail Russia's growing fleet.

buildings.name: Fur Trading Post
buildings.text: A frontier trading station where trappers bring pelts of sable, fox, and ermine to be collected, graded, and shipped to markets in Moscow and beyond.

children.text: The location's raw material is Fur
The location's raw material is Wild Game

buildings.name: Vodka Distillery
buildings.text: A grain spirit distillery producing the distinctive Russian liquor that generates significant revenue through state-controlled monopoly sales.

buildings.name: Forest Hermitage
buildings.text: A pustyn, a wilderness monastery of log cells around a wooden church. The monks clear the forest, the peasants who settle beside them clear more, and the pagan villages of the north hear the liturgy for the first time.

buildings.name: Cathedral of the East
buildings.text: A magnificent Orthodox cathedral built to consecrate Russia's claim as the Third Rome, rivaling the great churches of Constantinople and Rome in splendor.

buildings.name: Line Fortress
buildings.text: A bastioned fort of earth and timber on one of the fortified lines that the eighteenth century drew across southern Siberia, from Omsk up the Irtysh to Ust-Kamenogorsk. Its garrison holds the country behind it, where the fur tribute is gathered in peace.

list.name: Chamber of Genealogy
list.text: The chamber set up in 1682, when Tsar Feodor III burned the books of precedence by which the boyar clans had claimed commands according to the rank of their forebears. Every noble house hands in its descent, and the clerks enter it in a single register, bound in 1687 as the Velvet Book. The clans keep their honor on paper. When the register is neglected they dispute it again at court and at the muster.

list.name: Pomestie Registry
list.text: The conditional service-land system administered by the Razryadnyy Prikaz, granting estates (pomestiya) to mounted servitors in exchange for lifelong military duty. Unlike hereditary votchina, a pomestie reverted to the crown if its holder failed to muster, producing a salaried cavalry without the burden of cash pay. The registry's clerks tracked rolls, assigned grants, and over generations ratcheted the peasants tilling those lands ever closer to formal serfdom, culminating in the Ulozheniye of 1649.

list.name: D'iaki
list.text: The clerks of the Muscovite state. A d'iak is a man of common birth who learned his letters as an under-clerk in one of the offices at Moscow and rose by his pen. He is paid in coin and in land, he drafts every decree, and the highest of his kind sit in the Duma beside the boyars who are his betters by birth. Unpaid, he lives on what petitioners bring him.

list.name: Prikaz of Secret Affairs
list.text: The private office of Tsar Alexis, kept from 1654 until his death in 1676. It has a d'iak and a handful of clerks, and no boyar or man of the Duma may enter it. Its clerks ride beside ambassadors and governors and write to the tsar what they see, and through it he gives orders that pass no council. The great houses resent an office that watches them and answers to no one else.

conditions.text: Stability at least 0

list.name: Yamskaya Sluzhba
list.text: The postal relay system inherited by Muscovy from its Mongol overlords and formalized under the Yamskoy Prikaz, by which couriers bearing princely decrees rode in stages between yam stations spaced a day's ride apart along the great roads. The system carried orders from Moscow to the frontiers in days rather than weeks, knitting together a realm whose distances would otherwise have defied any centralized rule. It was sustained by a peasant corvee called the yamskaya povinnost', and its dense network of stations also doubled as a covert intelligence apparatus reporting on local affairs to the chancery.

list.name: Syshchiki
list.text: Commissioners sent from Moscow to the southern and eastern districts to find peasants who have fled their lords. Since the code of 1649 there is no limit of years on a claim: whoever is written in the census books is returned, with his children and his goods, to the estate or the monastery he left. The landlords are served, and the road out of bondage is closed.

conditions.text: Stability at least 1
